title: ED Triage Nursing Note
author: J. Castillo, RN
summary: EMS arrival 0400: known Addison disease, 2 days of vomiting/diarrhea, no steroid kept down; BP 78/44, HR 124, glucose 52, confused. ESI 1.
body:
**EMS report (Medic 14, arrival 0400)**
Husband called 911 at 0318: found her on the bathroom floor, confused and too weak to stand. On scene 0335: BP 74/40, HR 126, RR 22, SpO2 96% RA, temp 99.6 F, glucose 58. 18 g IV left antecubital, 500 mL saline wide open. Did not give oral glucose (vomiting, drowsy). Husband brought her medication bottles.

**Triage 0405**
T 99.8 F, HR 124, BP 78/44, RR 22, SpO2 97% RA, pain 6/10 crampy belly pain. POC glucose 52. ESI level 1.

**History from the husband (Daniel, health care proxy)**
- Addison disease (autoimmune adrenal insufficiency) since 2021; also Hashimoto hypothyroidism.
- Son had a "stomach bug" Friday. She started vomiting and having watery diarrhea Saturday afternoon (6-8 times a day).
- Vomited her hydrocortisone Saturday afternoon and Sunday morning; did not take extra doses. "She didn't know she was supposed to." No emergency injection kit at home. No medical alert bracelet.
- Dizzy when standing since Sunday evening, fell to her knees in the bathroom Sunday night (no head strike). Craving salt.

**Assessment**
Lethargic, opens eyes to voice, GCS 13. Oriented to self only. Skin warm, dry, tanned-looking; dark patches inside the cheeks and on the gums. Very dry mucous membranes. Weak thready radial pulses. Abdomen soft, diffusely tender.

**Actions**
Resuscitation room, cardiac monitor. Second IV 20 g right forearm 0406 with blood draw (BMP, CBC with differential, cortisol, ACTH, lactate, lipase, LFTs, TSH/free T4, troponin) BEFORE any steroid. Dr. Brennan at the bedside 0406.

title: ED Nursing Note - Treatments and Response
author: J. Castillo, RN
summary: D50 0408, hydrocortisone 100 mg IV 0420, NS 1 L x2, ondansetron 0430, D5NS 150 mL/h from 0600. BP 78/44 to 96/58, HR 124 to 104, glucose 52 to 96. More alert.
body:
**Treatments**
- 0406 labs drawn from the new 20 g right forearm IV (cortisol and ACTH included, ACTH on ice).
- 0408 dextrose 50% 25 g IV. Glucose 52 to 132 at 0425.
- 0415 sodium chloride 0.9% 1,000 mL over 30 minutes.
- 0420 hydrocortisone sodium succinate 100 mg IV push (Act-O-Vial), 14 minutes after the blood draw.
- 0425 12-lead ECG: sinus tachycardia 118, peaked T waves.
- 0430 ondansetron 4 mg IV; blood cultures x2.
- 0440 vomited 150 mL clear/bilious fluid. 0450 voided 150 mL dark yellow urine (UA, urine sodium and osmolality, urine hCG sent).
- 0450 sodium chloride 0.9% second 1,000 mL over 60 minutes.
- 0515 liquid brown stool 200 mL (no blood). Not sent (no order yet).
- 0600 D5NS at 150 mL/h.
- 0640 EMS IV (18 g left antecubital) was positional and leaking: removed; new 18 g left forearm placed, saline lock.

**Response**
0445 BP 86/50, HR 116. 0530 BP 92/54, HR 108, glucose 96. 0620 BP 96/58, HR 104, T 99.4 F. 0645 glucose 88.
More awake: answers questions, oriented to person and place. Still nauseated, belly cramps 4/10.

**Results**
Na 126, K 6.0, Cl 94, CO2 18, BUN 38, creatinine 1.6 (baseline 0.8), glucose 49 (before the D50), Ca 10.6. Eosinophils 7%. Lactate 3.1. Urine Na 48. Dr. Brennan aware of all.

**Family**
Husband at the bedside, very worried. Son (15) at home with a neighbor.

title: ED to Unit Handoff (SBAR)
author: J. Castillo, RN
summary: Handoff to 4 West RN: adrenal crisis improving after hydrocortisone 100 mg IV 0420 and 2.5 L fluid. Next hydrocortisone 1000. K 6.0 with peaked T waves, Na 126. Cortisol/ACTH pending.
body:
**S**
Lauren Mitchell, 46, known Addison disease, in adrenal crisis from 2 days of vomiting and diarrhea without her steroid. Coming to 4W-22 on telemetry.

**B**
Addison disease since 2021 on hydrocortisone 15 mg + 5 mg and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg; Hashimoto hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 88 mcg. No emergency kit at home. Allergy: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (hives). Full Code. Husband Daniel is her health care proxy.

**A**
Last vitals 0620: BP 96/58, HR 104 sinus tach, RR 18, SpO2 98% RA, T 99.4 F. Glucose 88 at 0645. Drowsy but answers, oriented to person and place. Nauseated, last vomit 0440. Liquid stool 0515. Voided 150 mL at 0450.
Labs: Na 126, K 6.0 (ECG 0425 peaked T waves), BUN 38, Cr 1.6, glucose 49 before D50, Ca 10.6. Cortisol and ACTH were drawn at 0406, BEFORE the hydrocortisone (0420); results pending.
In: EMS saline 500 + saline 2 L + D50 + D5NS = 2,700 mL. Out: 500 mL.
Lines: 20 g right forearm with D5NS 150 mL/h; 18 g left forearm saline lock; EMS line removed. Telemetry on.

**R**
- Hydrocortisone 50 mg IV every 6 hours: FIRST DOSE DUE 1000. Please give it on time.
- Glucose checks every 2 hours (0900 first); she dropped to 52 this morning.
- BMP every 4 hours from 0900. Watch the sodium: it should not rise more than 8 in 24 hours.
- Stool sample still needed (C. diff, GI panel); contact (enteric) precautions.
- Not safe to stand yet; fall precautions.
- Husband needs updates; she has not had any teaching on sick-day rules.
